src:
MOV     AH, 05h
MOV     CX, 48E0h        ; the grey Up arrow: scan 48h, E0h for "grey"
INT     16h
MOV     AH, 05h
MOV     CX, 8500h        ; F11: scan 85h
INT     16h
MOV     AH, 11h          ; enhanced check: is a key waiting?
INT     16h              ; ZF = 0, AX = 48E0h, left in the buffer
CALL    PHEX4
MOV     DL, " "
MOV     AH, 02h          ; DOS: print the character in DL
INT     21h
MOV     AH, 10h          ; enhanced read
INT     16h              ; 48E0h
CALL    PHEX4
MOV     DL, " "
MOV     AH, 02h          ; DOS: print the character in DL
INT     21h
MOV     AH, 10h
INT     16h              ; 8500h: F11
CALL    PHEX4
MOV     DL, " "
MOV     AH, 02h          ; DOS: print the character in DL
INT     21h
MOV     AH, 05h          ; the grey arrow once more...
MOV     CX, 48E0h
INT     16h
MOV     AH, 00h          ; ...read the old way
INT     16h              ; 4800h: it looks like the keypad arrow
CALL    PHEX4

PHEX4   PROC    NEAR     ; print AX as four hex digits; keeps every register
PUSH    AX
MOV     AL, AH
CALL    PHEX2            ; the high byte first
POP     AX
CALL    PHEX2            ; then the low byte
RET
PHEX4   ENDP
PHEX2   PROC    NEAR     ; print AL as two hex digits; keeps every register
PUSH    AX
PUSH    CX
PUSH    DX
MOV     DH, AL           ; keep the byte
MOV     CL, 4
SHR     AL, CL           ; the high nibble
CALL    HEXN1
MOV     AL, DH
AND     AL, 0Fh          ; the low nibble
CALL    HEXN1
POP     DX
POP     CX
POP     AX
RET
HEXN1:
ADD     AL, "0"
CMP     AL, "9"
JBE     HEXN2
ADD     AL, 7            ; past "9": "A".."F"
HEXN2:
MOV     DL, AL
MOV     AH, 02h
INT     21h
RET
PHEX2   ENDP
